There's source code and machine code. The source code is what people write to make a program that is then compiled into machine code that the computer uses. Source code is usually kept private unless it's an open source project. Machine code is what the user gets and is difficult to hack or reverse engineer. With the source code, programmers can now easily edit and remake the game and it's mechanics.

If you are looking for a fun Diablo tribute though, check out Path of Exile.

It's not really valuable in a commercial sense because anyone dumb enough to release a modified Diablo would be sued. Plus it's over 20 years old.

Diablo is a cult classic though. Having the full source code available is going to fascinate retro gamers and enthusiasts. It gives the person who did it a lot of street cred in that community too.

Most significantly, it means the entire game is entirely open to modification. When software is already compiled, it's often practically impossible to change even very minor things like one line of text. With the source code, however, you can make whatever changes you like and then compile the software for others to run. It means suitably motivated people could add new maps, missions, stories, weapons, whatever you can think of. They can fix bugs, add improved textures, etc. They can even completely reskin everything and make it about fairies and bunnies, constructing an entirely new game based on the Diablo engine. It's a (once) AAA title that any guy with a home PC can now build his own game on. It's old enough that this is doable.

It's a shit ton of work still though so we'll have to see what people with an awful lot of time and creativity do with it.
